**Reasoning:**

- **C3** is essentially a pure linear forward-speed reward (gated only by a soft uprightness factor), with negligible action/joint-velocity costs. Its marginal incentive for speed (≈1.0 per m/s) stays constant no matter how fast the ant gets, so the learning gradient never dies out — the logged `forward_speed` term is still climbing at a steady ~0.27/50 iters with no sign of saturation. It is the only candidate whose reward keeps pushing past the ~9–10 m/s region indefinitely.
- **C2** has the best *shape* (Gaussian tracking target at 9 m/s) and leads at iter 500 (task_score 7.54 ≈ mean forward speed), but its reward has an interior optimum: the tanh term is already saturated (1.88 of max 2.0), and the tracking bonus peaks at 9 m/s and then *decreases*, so its net gradient beyond ~9.5 m/s turns slightly negative. It will plateau around 9–10 m/s, i.e. it will be passed by C3 with 2,500 iterations remaining.
- **C1** has a very weak marginal gradient (0.2 linear + a tanh already at 0.46/0.6, temp 6 m/s) and its task_score growth has already flattened (only +0.10 in the last 50 iters) — it is saturating around 6–7 m/s.
- **C4** adds height/upright Gaussian preferences and a *quadratic* joint-velocity penalty that grows with gait speed, so the linear speed reward (1.0/m/s) is progressively cancelled; it grows slowest (~0.21/50) and starts last.

**Prediction (task_score ≈ mean forward velocity, so C3 keeps climbing while the others plateau):**

{"ranking": ["C3", "C2", "C1", "C4"]}
